summary: Iteration 128 (both backend + frontend) verification of the 2nd Goods-Issue follow-up fix: (1) try_post_goods_issue now groups still-open Outbound Delivery Request lines by parent_object_id and posts PGIInBackground ONCE per document; (2) new find_outbound_delivery_ids -> STO.outbound_delivery_ids (human-readable 'P8D1-185'); (3) StockTransferPage detail modal prefers the new plural list and falls back to the legacy singular object id. Updated (did NOT duplicate) the existing iteration_127 suite /app/backend/tests/test_sto_multi_item_gi_and_company_cache.py for the new per-DOCUMENT design: 29/29 pytest pass. All SAP interaction fully mocked - post_goods_issue was NEVER invoked against the live tenant (verified: every call in the suite goes to MockOutboundClient or a monkeypatched requests.get; no live SAP read either). Frontend verified live in the browser with a synthetic super_admin session: a seeded posted order with outbound_delivery_ids=['P8D1-185','P8D1-186'] renders 'Outbound Delivery: P8D1-185, P8D1-186' under data-testid=stock-transfer-detail-delivery-ids and does NOT show the legacy id; real pre-fix posted orders STO-000042 and STO-000045 gracefully fall back to 'Outbound Delivery Request: FA163E88...' with no blank/error. All temp data cleaned up.

minor.issue: No backfill for already-posted orders: gi_status=='posted' short-circuits at the top, and the 'all lines already Finished' early-return branch neither calls find_outbound_delivery_ids nor sets outbound_delivery_ids. Verified in Mongo that the very order the user complained about, STO-000046 (the real 3-line P8 order, deliveries P8D1-185/186/187), has outbound_delivery_object_ids populated but NO outbound_delivery_ids - so the user still will not see the human-readable Delivery IDs on that order (nor STO-000042/45). A one-off backfill (find_outbound_delivery_ids over the stored line UUIDs) or attempting the lookup in the all-Finished branch is needed for the fix to be visible on the orders that triggered it.

Insufficient-stock and delivery-ID-lookup handling is per-group, but the header still carries a single gi_status: when group A posts successfully and group B is short, gi_status becomes 'insufficient_stock' for the whole STO even though half the order has physically shipped (test_one_short_line_blocks_its_whole_group / test_finished_group_not_reposted_next_tick_and_ids_accumulate document this). Cosmetically confusing on the UI; consider a per-document status list.
A delivery item whose product_id matches no stored STO line is still posted with NO live stock pre-check (test_unmatched_product_line_does_not_block_group) - unchanged carry-over from iteration_127.

item_uuids are interpolated into the $filter without .upper() normalisation (find_delivery_request_items does upper-case its UUID) and without any chunking - a very wide STO would build one long 'or' filter. Not a defect today (SAP returned the expected rows for the real 3-line order per main agent's live check) but worth normalising/chunking.

critical_code_review_comments: Grouping logic is correct and defensive: groups.setdefault(d.get('parent_object_id') or d.get('object_id')) degrades to per-line posting rather than crashing if SAP ever omits ParentObjectID (covered by test_missing_parent_object_id_degrades_to_per_line).

A short line correctly blocks its ENTIRE document (no partial post) while a sibling document with full stock still posts - matches AllowSplitIndicator=false semantics and prevents recreating the multi-delivery bug.

find_outbound_delivery_ids failure is caught as SAPOutboundDeliveryError only and logged as a warning; gi_status stays 'posted' and outbound_delivery_ids stays [] so the next tick can retry (verified). Note: a non-SAP exception (e.g. AttributeError/ValueError) from that lookup would still bubble up and fail the whole job - a bare `except Exception` there would be safer for a purely cosmetic call.
Delivery IDs accumulate correctly across poll ticks (existing_delivery_ids | fresh_ids, sorted) - a second group's post does not wipe the first group's ID.

stock_transfer_service.py is 1007 lines and sap_outbound_delivery_client.py carries ~60 lines of incident narrative in its docstring; consider splitting the Goods-Issue polling logic into its own module.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the user's 3-separate-deliveries report: PGIInBackground was called once per Outbound Delivery Request ITEM ObjectID, and SAP creates one Outbound Delivery per call. Fix verified: pending lines are grouped by their shared ParentObjectID (the Outbound Delivery Request DOCUMENT) and PGIInBackground is called exactly once per distinct parent (3 lines/1 parent -> 1 call with the parent id; 2 parents -> exactly 2 calls, each scoped to its own group; a short line suppresses its whole group only; a group already Finished ('3') is not re-posted on a later tick). Fix 2 verified: find_outbound_delivery_ids filters OutboundDeliveryItemBusinessTransactionDocumentReferenceOutboundDeliveryRequestC on ItemUUID (not UUID) with $expand=OutboundDelivery and returns de-duplicated .ID values; the service merges them into outbound_delivery_ids without losing earlier groups', and a lookup failure leaves gi_status='posted'. Remaining gap: no backfill for orders posted before the fix, so STO-000046 still shows no Delivery ID in the UI.
